If you're a pinball fan, Fantastic Journey is a pretty amazing feat, and the price is definitely right.
The game just doesn't have enough substance to last more than a day.
This game truly makes me wonder if the original was really that much fun or if I was just too young to care.
You still pick one of three monsters and blow up every building in sight.
Even the multiplayer-crazed "party game" crowd won't find any nuggets of gaming goodness here.
Hasbro Interactive has successfully "ported" one of the oldest and most popular turn-based strategy games to the PlayStation.
Williams has done well to go back to its roots, because this time it has come up with a winner.
Rollaway is a great game that offers just about all the addiction, frustration, and satisfaction a puzzle fan could ask for
Aside from R-Type fans, the casual gamer might find this game too hard and with not enough reward.
Scrabble on the PlayStation appears to be exactly what you expect from Scrabble at your mom's house - minus the little wooden letters that look like bouillon cubes.
From the beginning of the manual, to the design of the Sentinel itself, so much is made of the game's surrealism, it seems like an alibi for the lack of any palpably realistic environment.
Fun in a low-key way.
The lame minigames, lack of varied speech, and generally slow pace of the game make it short-lived fun at best.
If classic games are what you're after, get a pack of classic games, or better yet, find a big arcade that still cares about the old stuff.
Wait for the next album, the next movie, the next TV special, or whatever. But don't bother buying this game.
Spin Jam is decidedly unique, and it may make a good purchase for puzzle fans looking for something fresh.
Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo earns big points for style.
No amount of multimedia candy can save this game from its main flaw: boredom.
It responds just as you would expect it to respond and puts on a pretty good act. But it is an act.
If you didn't play Parappa to death and love every minute of it, you might as well skip out on Um Jammer Lammy.

games.title: Who Wants To Be A Millionaire Second Edition

review.blurb: Who Wants to be A Millionaire doesn't have a terribly large bank of questions to choose from, and you'll probably start to recognize a few questions after only three or four sessions.

games.title: Who Wants To Be A Millionaire Third Edition

review.blurb: If you're into trivia games like You Don't Know Jack, you may get some mileage out of Who Wants To Be A Millionaire, but its uninteresting gameplay and methodical pacing make it practically a chore to play.
Although the game has its weak points, the solid gameplay and simple control make this game a must-have for anyone who likes to play games with other humans.
It's definitely a great multiplayer party-style game.
You Don't Know Jack: Mock 2 is instant fun for just about anyone that likes trivia.
Being able to play with all the physical cards you own makes this game the ideal companion piece for avid collectors who want to see their cards duke it out in 3D.
An addictive, well-rounded game that is balanced, challenging, and, most of all, fun to play.
The Arc the Lad Collection is ultimately an interesting, varied, and rewarding experience that has a tendency to sometimes get bogged down.
With each successive RPG, Konami has gotten bolder and braver.
Bastard!! truly defines the term mish-mash.
Beyond the Beyond lands squarely in familiar territory - nothing likely to convert new players.
Even with its handful of new features, Breath of Fire III breaks little new ground.
Breath of Fire IV is as solid a game as any of its predecessors.
Gamers looking for a simple, inoffensive, and remarkably replayable RPG may find solace in the dark, dank, and old-fashioned recesses of Square's dungeons.
Chrono Cross may not have had the largest budget, but it has the largest heart.
Darkstone makes an excellent case for making a modest $10 investment.
Blizzard's Diablo, winner of GameSpot's PC Game of the Year for 1996, has finally made it onto the PlayStation.
Even with its budget-minded pricing, Digimon World 3 is at best an average role-playing game that will appeal only to fans of the greater Digimon franchise.
The branching family tree adds a measure of replay value, but the game is average enough that few will want to play it through more than once.
If you know you're in the market for a very lengthy and ultimately satisfying RPG and know you can get over the visuals, you owe it to yourself to give Dragon Warrior VII a try.
Final Fantasy IV looks most dated by today's standards.
Never before have technology, playability, and narrative combined as well as in Final Fantasy VII.
Cast all fears aside: the latest Final Fantasy is the greatest game ever to bear the name.
Final Fantasy IX serves as a coda to the series as you know it - it's a summation of everything that players have enjoyed about the past ten years of Final Fantasy games.
Mediocre packaging and emulation quirks aside, it's hard not to like Final Fantasy Anthology.
Final Fantasy IV and Chrono Trigger represent some of the best that the Square of old had to offer.
The two games included in Final Fantasy Origins may be short on presentation, but they're certainly long enough on gameplay to justify the purchase price for any hard-core RPG fan.
Grandia is every bit as worthwhile as Final Fantasy VIII, just in different ways.
This hack-and-slash action/role-playing game is pleasant, but it just doesn't live up to its ambition and ends up feeling small and empty.
Guardian's Crusade never pretends to be anything besides an enjoyable RPG.
For fans of the original manga, this is a must-buy.
Those looking for a game with hours and hours of highly addictive, nonviolent gameplay should find a comfortable chair and a copy of Harvest Moon: Back to Nature.
Jade Cocoon is easily one of the best-looking games of the year.
The unfaltering polygonal consistency of King's Field is mesmerizing after extended play.
The first King's Field was an excellent game, and its like-minded sequel is even better.
Overall, Koudelka falls short of expectations in the gameplay department, but the beautiful CG work in the game's movies definitely makes the experience a memorable one.
While it's a good first try, Sony's inexperience with the genre shows through, resulting in a highly generic RPG with some out-of-this-world FMV.
Despite the little flaws that keep Legaia from being the world beater that it could have been, it still remains an engaging RPG for anyone who likes to play RPGs.
A string of miniquests without a cohesive core, Legend of Mana is likely to disappoint fans hoping for a new action RPG classic, but it will entertain those just looking for a good time.
Those with a tolerance or desire for older games and the nostalgia inherent in them will definitely want to give Lunar 2 a shot.
Lunar may not have modern aesthetics, but its gameplay and story are among the best of any RPG of any era.
However it happened, Blam!'s pure intentions went chaotically awry, resulting in one of the worst PlayStation games in recent memory.
Expect to finish the game all the way through in no more than 15 hours.
Altus' Persona for the PlayStation easily qualifies as a sleeper hit.

RPG fans looking for something other than the standard "boy meets girl, boy loses girl in heart-wrenching cutscene, boy avenges girl's death and saves world" formula should definitely give Persona 2 a shot.

IMPORT: Persona 2: Innocent Sin is a rare gem in today's RPG market - despite the popularization of the genre, it's stayed true to its offbeat roots to deliver a story, setting, and style unlike anything you're likely to have played before.
If you're the type of RPGer who commits to checking out the most nonstandard manifestations of the genre, then Rhapsody is definitely worth your attention.

Knowing off the bat that your experience with RPG Maker will frequently have you elbow-deep in the most hostile of interfaces - scripting events, penning text, or what have you - will most adequately prepare you for the rigors of RPG making.
SaGa Frontier is a solid, if not exactly stellar, RPG.
SaGa Frontier 2 will likely please RPG fans who are able to overlook the first title's looming shadow.
Despite its age, the title is well executed and possesses enough merit to compete in the market in 2001.
Whoever said "Graphics don't matter" never played Shadow Madness.
The game looks extremely outdated when compared with current PlayStation games.
Star Ocean might not be compelling enough to play through twice, but the first time is as engaging as any RPG you're likely to play.
Though Suikoden may not be groundbreaking, it's definitely good.
Suikoden II brings nothing new to the genre, but it executes well enough that no one will really care.
While the game is new to US gamers, Tactics Ogre will be a blast from the past for just about everyone.
Namco's Tales of Destiny is one of those RPGs that should've been left abroad.
If you value the gameplay that really makes an RPG what it is, you'll find a lot to like in Tales of Destiny II.
The game has a strong anime aesthetic - sometimes cute, sometimes wacky, and definitely attractive.
Expert RPG fans will likely blow straight through this game without a single setback.
Torneko is a charming little adventure that manages to push the nostalgia button without feeling overly dated.
While a fairly short game, the depth and density of the story and gameplay contained in Vagrant Story give it an intensity missing from most longer games.

Valkyrie Profile is a complex, ambitious, and gorgeous title that offers much to like: beautiful aesthetics, an entertaining battle system, engaging characters, and a creatively balanced "dual" scenario.
This battlefield strategy RPG isn't for everyone, but if you're a strategy RPG fan that isn't too fussy about graphics, you'll be pleased.
Every fan of RPG games should at least take a peek at this title.
Wild Arms 2 isn't bad, but it doesn't begin to approach today's standard of good, either.
Xenogears' reliance on story, subtlety, and mood make it Square's most anime-like RPG thus far, in many ways making the game one of its best.
Zill O'll is Koei's Final Fantasy.
Ace Combat 2 fixes every problem that troubled the first game.
Darklight Conflict presents good space combat with nice visuals.
Eagle One does have its problems, but in the end, it's not a total loss.
Macross VF-X ultimately fails to capture the emotion, the excitement, and the sheer visual splendor of its source material.
Other mech games may claim to be a great combination of simulation and action, but only MechWarrior 2 comes close to the mark.
Overall, X Games Pro Boarder is the best snowboarding game out for the PlayStation.
FIFA 2002 is still the better soccer game for the PlayStation--unless you're a World Cup fanatic.
Even NASCAR fans will cringe when their character slams to the asphalt with a fleshy "smack."
This is by far the best-looking baseball video game to date.
After playing the game for 30 minutes you'll be wishing you had rented something else.
In the end, Action Bass is a solid arcade-style fishing game that the majority of armchair anglers will enjoy.
Adidas Power Soccer rises high above the standard soccer fare.
Adidas Power Soccer 98 does a number of things well, but its shortcomings are frustrating enough to turn most players off before the whistle blows.
Even the die-hard soccer fan will want to skip this one.
A feature-heavy game that has adequate play control and graphics.
It's the most complete pool-simulation game around for the PlayStation.
Ballblazer Champions has everything that a remake could want.
Baseball 2000 feels, plays, and looks just the way its name sounds: generic.
Bass Rise makes for an amusing diversion best suited for casual fishing fans who generally play for no longer than an hour per sitting.
There's just no need for a game like this on the PlayStation in 1997.
Certainly this is not an offensive game by any means, but it's remarkably average.
The money spent on this game would be better spent playing a real game of pool.
Overall, Bottom of the Ninth is a fair baseball title. But when it comes to sports games, fair isn't what you're looking for.
It comes as no surprise that the $10 you would spend on purchasing this game would be better spent on several games at a real bowling alley.
Boxing is just simply a fun game to play that is more than worth its $10 price tag.
Even if you aren't a bowling fan, and couldn't care less about this game, you really should see the video clips at least once.
Brunswick Circuit Pro Bowling 2 is accurate enough to keep die-hard rollers happy, yet simple enough to be a game even a casual bowling fan would enjoy.
Although it lacks enough bells and whistles to snag mainstream gamers who aren't into the sport, it packs enough excitement to warrant long-term commitment by fishing fans.
It's a solid game that's fun to watch, but it's no longer the only game in town.
While far from perfect, it is easily the best surfing game on the market, but more importantly, it's also a fun game.
It may not have real fighters or venues, but it plays well and looks decent.
Contender 2 is a much more enjoyable arcade-style boxing game than its processor, and fans of the original game, as well as fans of the genre, will undoubtedly enjoy it.
More than a great snowboarding game, it's a pretty good racer as well.
Cool Boarders 2 is an awesome snowboarding game.
From both a technical and aesthetic standpoint, Cool Boarders 2001 is like a winter without snow - a drag.
Unfortunately, Cool Boarders 3 isn't the sequel we had all hoped for - changing developers for this third game really hurt the series a lot.
CB4 is basically a better version of CB3.

The single most obvious characteristic you'll discover within the first five minutes of playing CyberTiger was that if the game had come out before Hot Shots Golf or even before Mario Golf, it might have been more impressive.

games.title: Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX: Maximum Remix

review.blurb: The graphics in Maximum Remix are roughly identical to the first game, so you're stuck with muddy, ugly textures and quite a bit of texture warping.
The only major flaw in Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX is that the game is a touch on the easy side.
While Anarchy Rulz bears the ECW logo, the wrestling action is simply too low impact and refined for the likes of this brutal organization.
ECW and its fans deserve better than this.

Konami has gone to great lengths to integrate two- and four-player capability into each of the game's non-season modes, which opens up the possibility of introducing your sports-phobic friends to a soccer game they can actually play.
FIFA 2000 is more than just better than last year's game, it is easily the best soccer game ever to grace the PlayStation.
Though FIFA 2001 is a solid enough game in its own right, the game's lack of innovation or significant upgrades keeps it from having the same impact as FIFA 2000.
The PlayStation version of FIFA 2002 doesn't quite have all the features available on the PlayStation 2, but it makes a solid case for an investment on its own.
While not completely perfect, it's deep on options, packed with real teams and players, and presented with a slick interface.
EA has delivered a serious soccer game for serious soccer players.
There's a deep, dark secret in this industry.
In the grand tradition of licensed games, this one also falls far short of being interesting or fun to play.
It's more often than not that a sports game fails to live up to gamers' expectations, and with just cause.
Though not without a handful of control issues and flaws in commentary, the freshness of Fox's approach makes for a great game.
A big meal that has all the trimmings but somehow manages to leave you unsatisfied.
HBO Boxing is another disappointing boxing game that fails to even come close to re-creating the look and feel of the sport in the ring.
High Heat Baseball 2000 is easily the worst baseball game to come out for the PlayStation this year.
While the game isn't bad by any means, it just doesn't stand up to the other games on the market.
In a move bound to please golf enthusiasts and curious onlookers alike, Sony has brought its flagship golf game to our shores under the moniker of Hot Shots Golf.
Hot Shots Golf 2 has some big shoes to fill. But not only does it fill those shoes, it also stretches them a little - as Hot Shots Golf 2 is more than a worthy successor to the original.
If you're a fan of multiplayer games, this is definitely one to check out.
K-1 Grand Prix is for the most part the same as the original.
This sequel falls squarely into the rent-me bin.
In the final analysis, K1 is a perfect game to rent for a couple nights.
Overall, Knockout Kings is the best representation of the sport of boxing in a game so far.

Die-hard boxing purists who are still looking for a game with true-to-life gameplay, however, will enjoy Knockout Kings 2000 for a brief period, quickly tire of its sim-free control, and keep looking.
Knockout Kings 2001 is easily the best iteration of the series thus far, thanks to improved AI, cleaner graphics, and tighter controls.
KO The Live Boxing is the latest of the Japanese boxing games that combines the simulation aspects of Boxer's Road with the 3D action of Center Ring Boxing, but not very well.
It's a scaled-down version of Blitz 2000 with a few changes, but these changes don't really enhance the game in any way - unless you're a die-hard Arena Football fan, of course.
Libero Grande is, without a doubt, an unapologetic arcade soccer experience, making no pretenses to heavy stat-tracking or any of that kind of tomfoolery.
Fans of the series will undoubtedly call Madden NFL 2000 the best incarnation of the series thus far.
Madden NFL 2001 is arguably the most entertaining two-player sports game ever made.
While Madden 2002 isn't reinventing football on the PlayStation, it is really the best you're going to get on the system.
For a first effort, EA's Madden NFL 97 is a fine offering.
Although it doesn't have flashy 3D graphics, Madden 98 is still the most realistic and complete football game on the market.
New animations, like receivers tracking the ball with their head, really give the players a life of their own.
It's obvious that the March Madness development team did its homework.
The soundtrack rivals Wipeout XL for the title of best licensed soundtrack ever.
Mike Tyson's Boxing just doesn't have the depth of Knockout Kings or the immediate satisfaction found from the arcade style of play in Ready 2 Rumble.
Other than a few minor modes and some touched-up graphics, MLB 2K is the same game as MLB 99.
Pacing and sound issues aside, 989 Studios has fixed many of the glaring flaws of last year's release and as such has created a game superior to EA's offering.
If you can get past the sluggish pacing and incessant overcomplication, MLB 2002 is a wonderful game.
If you must have a baseball game that features the latest player rosters and you're bound to the old PlayStation, MLB 2003 is the best and only choice.
MLB 2004 is a solid, complete baseball game, even if many of you have seen it before.
Sony seems to have put a lot into this game, but it lacks polish.
MLB 99 is a sound baseball game, and fans of last year's MLB 98 will surely enjoy it.
Sony's new Playstation-exclusive MLB Pennant Race is an excellent baseball sim that offers more options than any of its console competitors.
MTV: Pure Ride is an excellent snowboarding game, but it's yet another example of a development house shifting the majority of its resources to the next generation of hardware.

games.title: MTV Sports: Skateboarding featuring Andy Macdonald

review.blurb: MTV Skateboarding is a perfect example of cashing in on a recently established genre, yet unlike games like Street Sk8er 2 or Grind Session, it doesn't bring anything worthwhile to the table.
If you were a fan of X Games Pro Boarder, then you'll definitely like MTV Sports: Snowboarding since it's really the "unofficial" sequel.

games.title: MTV Sports: T.J. Lavin�s Ultimate BMX

review.blurb: Landing vert tricks and pulling off long grinds can be a chore, because the game has a seemingly random system of determining whether or not your bike is straight enough to land. A coin toss would be more predictable.
Nagano '98 should be avoided at all costs.
NBA Basketball 2000 is a great first effort from Fox Interactive, but, unfortunately, it looks better than it plays.
NBA Fastbreak '98 packs most of the play options from other games into one, and the result is a pretty good first attempt.
This version of NBA Hangtime falls very short of expectations.
While still fun in head-to-head situations, the few added features can't mask the fact that NBA Hoopz is basically the same exact game as last year's NBA Showtime.
NBA In The Zone 2 sets a new standard of visual excellence for sports games on any console system.
When playing against other people, NBA In The Zone '98 is pretty fun.
The well-drawn graphics are perhaps the game's strongest point, especially in the dunks and instant replays.
What really makes this, and all other NBA Jam games, worthwhile are the hidden features.
Fans of previous versions of Live will have a good time.
NBA Live 2001 follows the fine tradition established by previous versions while adding just about every conceivable gameplay option.
NBA Live 97 may very well be the best Playstation-based basketball game to date.
NBA Live 98 is an improvement over Live 97 in almost every category.
The NBA season may still be in jeopardy, but Live is open for business and always ready for a game.
Its clean graphics and great control not only make it the best installment in the Shootout series but also one of the best basketball games for the PlayStation.
989 has opted to take the easy road this time around, and the result is a basketball game that remains virtually unchanged from last year's version.
NBA ShootOut 2002 is virtually identical to last year's game.
NBA Shoot Out '97 has been significantly improved over last year's premiere.
Compared with other basketball titles out this year, ShootOut 98 is at the bottom of the pile.
It's not perfect, but NBA Showtime is still a fun four-player game, and it's worlds better than any other arcade basketball game on the PlayStation.
In the end, NCAA Final Four is a step above average.
While NCAA Final Four 2000 isn't by any means the best basketball game for the PlayStation, it is a sound college basketball game.

NCCA Final Four 2001 features relatively entertaining arcade-style hoops action, but the game's subpar graphics, lack of options, annoying control flaws, and lack of on-court atmosphere keep it from meeting those expectations.
A game that most casual fans would probably be willing to settle for.
While its not leaps and bounds beyond the previous game, all of the other little extras make it well worth your money.
Is NCAA 2001 different than last year's title, or the year before that? Nope, it's pretty much the same experience with a few new tricks.
NCAA 98 is the perfect game for college football fanatics.
It's a pretty complete game and one that should satisfy just about any college football fan.
GameBreaker is knocked out of the game thanks to its atrocious playbook interface.
Casual fans may not notice all the little nuances, plays, and animations, but fans of the Gamebreaker series surely will.
NCAA GameBreaker 2001 is basically the same as last year's model.
Football fans with an open mind or just the thirst for something new should definitely put GameBreaker 99 through its paces.
The game controls well, looks good, and, most importantly, it's a whole lot of fun.
EA added the new coach mode and polished an already stellar game into the best college hoops simulation for the PlayStation.
March Madness 99 is the most complete college hoops sim available, but the game's slow-paced gameplay is a black mark on its record.
Blitz is the most addictive sports game ever created.
NFL Blitz 2000 still has a firm lock on the arcade football business.
NFL Blitz 2001 takes a low-key approach, delivering much the same features as last year's release while offering a number of minor refinements in key areas.
All the new animations, plays, and GM features really make Gameday 2000 the best Gameday yet.
In the end, GameDay 2001, aside from its obvious roster updates and a few minor additions, is totally identical to last year's title, which was a really good game.
GameDay 2002 does a decent job of delivering a fun and somewhat realistic game of football to the PlayStation.
There is enough solid gameplay to make this the best football game around, on any system.
NFL GameDay '98 is a great technical feat and a very fun football game.
In the end GameDay 99 is the total package.
While this game has some admirable qualities, in the end it falls short of the high standards set by Madden '97.
NFL Xtreme is no NFL Blitz.
If you're thinking about buying NFL Xtreme 2, the answer is really quite simple. Don't.
NHL 2000 is the best PlayStation version of the series thus far.
While it's not the most beautiful hockey video game, NHL 2001 comes through where it counts - the gameplay.
NHL 98 is among the best.
It may still be a bit sluggish on the frame rate side, but if you're a fan of previous NHL titles, you won't be disappointed.
Blades of Steel 2000 for the PlayStation fails to deliver a hockey experience that could be considered better than any one of its competitors.
A true 32-bit hockey game has finally arrived.
The play-by-play and pregame announcing by Fox Sports announcers John Davidson and Kenny Albert is really great.
If FaceOff's brand of hockey wasn't your bag last year, this year is likely to be an instant replay.
If you own either of the past two renditions of NHL FaceOff, you really have no reason to pick up 2001.
Despite a few quirks, this is an excellent hockey game with abundant options, pinpoint control, and sharp graphics.
All in all, FaceOff is simply average.
NHL 99 is easily the better choice.
Complete with all the detail, realism, and pro licenses anyone could expect from a quality sports sim.
With realistic hockey sims a dime a dozen on the Playstation, Open Ice is a welcome and refreshing change.
All in all, Powerplay '96 is just another average hockey game.
You'd probably be better served by NHL 98 or NHL Breakaway '98.

Hockey fans may find that the game strays a bit too far from their favorite sport, but the game is amazingly exciting and makes a worthwhile purchase for anyone looking for a fast-paced competitive game.
Golden Tee Golf doesn't contain anything that warrants a recommendation.
With PGA Tour 97, EA Sports has released rehash.
Pitball is an excellent game, containing more options and gameplay challenges than most "real" sports simulations.
For snowmobile fans with a little extra cash to burn, Polaris SnoCross proves to be a rather entertaining diversion as long as you can accept its odd collision glitches.
While it's a good game, Pool Hustler is a few steps short of what Backstreet Billiards has to offer.
While Powermove's gameplay elements are solid for the most part, the game lacks any real personality or lasting appeal.
Power Spike Pro Beach Volleyball makes a good attempt, but its inconsistencies and shoddy control detract from the overall experience.
Pro 18: World Tour Golf isn't necessarily a bad golf game - it's just that so many other PlayStation golf games make the experience more fun.
Professional Underground League of Pain represents video gaming's latest trend: beautifully shaded graphics and lush stereo sound contrasted with poor game play.
The ability it gives you to throw your own combos surpasses the combo system used in Knockout Kings 2000
Ready 2 Rumble: Round 2 has more boxers and moves than the first game, but aside from a few slight changes here and there, the game remains largely unchanged.
Whether you love real fishing or not, you'll probably hate Reel Fishing.
Rushdown seems as though it could have been a passable game - three years ago.
The gameplay is decent, many of last year's aggravating flaws are nowhere to be found, and the general feel of a baseball game is present.
The sheer lack of quality throughout the game keeps Sammy Sosa's Softball Slam from being anything interesting.
Smash Court 2 is the sequel to Namco's little known tennis game, Smash Court, which was originally released in Japan back in 1996.
Sno-Cross Championship Racing, a quality game based entirely on snowmobile racing, proves that there's no good reason for the unvaried focus of today's racing games.
Despite the use of much-loved Warner Bros. cartoon characters, Space Jam fails miserably in every category.
Even though it's not quite up to prevailing standards, Speedball 2100 still packs quite a bit of wallop.
Streak is surprisingly rough around the edges for a third-generation racing game.
It's in the gameplay that Street Sk8er really falls flat.
Street Sk8er 2 is a huge improvement over the original, and skaters looking for something to do while waiting for Tony Hawk 2 to ship would do well to check out EA's second offering.
With so much competition on the PS it's tough to recommend Striker Pro 2000 over FIFA or ISS.
A mere $40 investment stands between you and one of the best arcade-style motorcycle racing games the PlayStation has to offer.
Super Shot Soccer is a pretty fun game that's a little short on options but not bad on offering up some well-rounded soccer gameplay.

In the end, Surf Riders is a fun game with decent gameplay, but the shortage of modes, run-of-the-mill graphics, and lack of variety prevent Surf Riders from being to surf games what Tony Hawk's Pro Skater is to skateboarding games.
If you buy into the whole button-mashing mentality of track and field games, you'll find that Sydney 2000 turns in a solid, finger-numbing performance.
With no stat tweaking and no licenses, Tennis Arena is arcade-style tennis at its most fundamental.
This game isn't as fun as real bowling - it's more fun than real bowling.
While this may not be the best golf video game ever, it's easily one of the better offerings available on the Playstation.
If you're finished with Tony Hawk, and you're hungry for another challenge, Thrasher: Skate and Destroy is the meal you're looking for.
Although arriving on the scene later than some other golf games, Tiger Woods 99 is still as good a golf sim as you're likely to find.

Even Tiger Woods himself can't save Tiger Woods PGA Tour 2000 from being a game so bland that even the most immobile of golf fans will rather dust off their spiked shoes than settle with this year's offering.
Those simply looking for a good PlayStation golf game are better off looking at the Hot Shots series than picking up this antiquated, middle-of-the-road golf game.
It's one of those games that will keep you coming back long after you've mastered it.

As most major publishers' development efforts shift to any number of next-generation platforms, Tony Hawk 2 will likely stand as one of the last truly fantastic games to be released on the PlayStation.
If you're not ready to commit to the PlayStation 2 yet, and you've grown weary of the levels in Tony Hawk 2, then Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 is just the ticket.
While Trick'n Snowboarder may not pack enough original mojo to rise far above other well-known titles in its genre, it plays fast and looks good.
Triple Play 2000 is a welcome addition to the PlayStation baseball lineup that everyone, even those who weren't fans of previous Triple Play games, should check out.
Though hard-core fans may scoff at the addition of rewards and cheats, the option to play without them makes Triple Play 2001 an update that both simulation fans and arcade lovers can embrace.
Pinpoint control, and picture-perfect stadiums, this is a diamond lover's dream.
Triple Play's new 3-D graphics look absolutely stunning.
Triple Play 99 is the way to go if you want a realistic baseball sim to play.
Triple Play Baseball is one of those rare games that really draws you into the experience with fantastic gameplay and quality graphics and sound.
Ever wanted to play pool against Satan? Hey, who hasn't?
Virtual Pool is no hustle.
VR Sports has managed to deliver a miserable failure.
The game just doesn't have the polished look of Triple Play or MLB.
The game barely scratches the surface of what the Playstation game machine can do.
In the final analysis, suffice to say that other soccer sims do it better for the same price.
EA's Backstage Assault is a novel idea, but in the end, it doesn't have enough variation to make it worthwhile.
Despite its flaws, WCW Mayhem still manages to be a really fun game, and it is definitely worth picking up.
Even with its graphical difficulties, WCW Nitro is still the best WCW-licensed wrestling game out there.
While Thunder does a good job of looking like real wrestling, the gameplay just doesn't hold up.
All in all, WCW is a solid wrestling game.
On the basis of AI improvements alone, World Cup 98 is highly recommended.
Attitude succeeds because War Zone was an excellent wrestling game.
WWF In Your House is a dated effort barely worthy of the 32-bit age.
The little things that debut in SmackDown, such as a never-ending season mode and inklings of a plot, really make the game feel fresh and new.
While it isn't that much different from the last SmackDown!, SmackDown! 2 makes enough incremental changes and upgrades to be significant in its own right.
While WWF War Zone plays similarly to its predecessors, it presents a package that is completely unmatched in both gameplay and in atmosphere.
The term "Armchair General" was coined for this kind of game.
Battle Hunter is an easy-to-learn, yet addictive, trek into dungeon-based treasure collecting and RPG-style character development.
A real-time Battleship for the 90s.
Blast Chamber could have used more time in the oven.
